items.title: Thailand Keeps Building for Tourists Who May Not Come
items.summary: Thailand’s arrivals outlook has weakened, but new rooms and flights are still coming. The test is whether resilient luxury demand and new source markets can deliver the returns that investors want.

items.title: Wyndham Launches Homes & Havens to Take On Marriott
items.summary: Whether Wyndham's Homes & Havens can compete with Marriott's far larger collection is an open question. But for Wyndham, this is only day one.

items.title: Hyatt Raises Outlook, but Its All-Inclusives Lag
items.summary: When affluent travelers spend, Hyatt wins. The catch is that a portfolio built on luxury leisure is a bet on the wealth effect, and the good times could end if the stock market sneezes.

items.title: Norwegian Cruise Line’s Turnaround Shows Early Traction After Activist Shakeup
items.summary: Better close-in demand, cost cuts, and second-half 2027 bookings on par with last year at higher prices suggest Norwegian Cruise Line's turnaround plan is starting to take hold, but the company still trails rivals that are already growing yields.

items.title: IndiGo’s Willie Walsh Wants More Revenue From Every Passenger
items.summary: IndiGo’s answer to losing passengers is the Ryanair model of earning more from each one. But Ryanair’s extras depend on European rules. Walsh himself concedes India’s rules do put limits on that playbook.

items.title: Which Airlines Are Still Skipping Dubai This Winter
items.summary: Dubai’s airport is busy, but the long-haul airlines that fill its luxury hotels are mostly staying out until spring. Hotels organizing around a European winter rebound need to plan for a later one.

items.title: MGM Resorts Sees Lost Pricing Power in Las Vegas as Travel Costs Bite
items.summary: Higher transportation costs appear to be squeezing Las Vegas hotels’ pricing power. Yet convention business has helped offset weaker leisure demand in some months

items.title: Why AI Agents Could Become Travel’s New Digital Front Door: Watch Video
items.summary: At Skift Global Forum, Sierra CEO Bret Taylor argued that AI agents could connect booking, service, sales, and loyalty into a more seamless customer relationship, organized around the traveler rather than a company’s internal structure.
